local_articles.title: Miami Marlins' Kyle Stowers hits home run to beat Philadelphia Phillies 1-0 in 2nd straight win
local_articles.snippet: Sandy Alcantara pitched four-hit ball over seven sharp innings, Kyle Stowers homered and the Miami Marlins beat the Philadelphia Phillies 1-0 on Tuesday night. Xavier Edwards singled and had two walks, and Liam Hicks had two hits for the Marlins, who won their second straight after ending a franchise-record 12-game losing streak Monday. Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber, who leads the National League with 33 homers, didn't play because of a gastrointestinal illness. Alcantara (11-6) struck out five and walked one. It was Alcantara's major league-leading 16th quality start and the 111th of his career, surpassing Ricky Nolasco for the franchise record. Calvin Faucher relieved Alcantara and thew a perfect eighth before Pete Fairbanks closed with another perfect inning for his 14th save. The Marlins struck quickly on Stowers' blast in the first. local_articles.title: Miami Marlins defeat Philadelphia Phillies 8-6, overcoming losses and marking their largest comeback of the season
local_articles.snippet: Griffin Conine hit a go-ahead pinch-hit homer in the eighth, Otto Lopez, Heriberto Hernández and Xavier Edwards each had two RBIs, and the Miami Marlins rallied to beat the Philadelphia Phillies 8-6 on Wednesday. The Marlins overcame a 6-0 deficit to mark their largest comeback of the season. They had previously rallied from four runs down on May 9 against the Nationals, and have come back 21 times this year. Lopez got the Marlins on the board in the fifth, grounding out but driving in Esteury Ruiz to make it 6-1. Hernández then sent a high changeup from Jesús Luzardo 416 feet to left-center to get the Fightin' Fish within three. Lopez drove in another with a single in the seventh and Edwards drove in two more with a single of his own to tie the game at 6-all. local_articles.snippet: But this young talent won't be coming to Detroit much longer. The tournament won't be part of the 2027 season as the PGA Tour continues to reshape its schedule. "I mean, it's sad to see the tournament not being here next year," Potgieter said. local_articles.title: Pro golfers meet up for Par 3 in the D ahead of Rocket Classic
local_articles.snippet: Downtown Detroit turned into a golf course Tuesday evening for the Par 3 in the D event promoting the final Rocket Classic. "We've seen them down the street at the golf course, but didn't think they'd be shooting over Woodward, so that's why we came down," said golf fan David Graciak. Six of the best golfers in the world teed off from the top of the historic five-story UBS Building and sent golf balls flying off the building and onto a custom-built green below across Woodward. "Dan Gilbert tasked us with making the final Rocket Classic the biggest and best one yet, and kicking it off with par 3 in the d is the only way we knew how to do it," said Dean Bokuniewicz, the director of marketing for Rocket Classic. questions.title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: Updated on 2026-07-28 incorporating AP syndication confirmation, DHS statistical-reporting risk, and TRAC analysis: (1) AP wire coverage (via Iola Register July 21) explicitly uses ICE's July 20 Detention Management book-ins dataset showing >43,000 arrests in June (43,138, beating Dec 2025's 42,107 and every month Jan-May 2026) and 1,593/day in July 1-11 (~49k pace), cutting January's alternate-series edge case 0.04 -> 0.01; (2) no new ICE update arrived by July 28 (next biweekly cycle is Aug 3, which with a ~9-day lag would likely only cover through ~July 25, meaning full-month July requires an Aug 10-24 release); (3) USA Today (July 21) noted ICE's average gap between releases stretched to 42 days in 2026, and today (July 28 Daily Beast) DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics executive director Marc Rosenblum resigned citing downsizing and 'war on facts,' modestly elevating the risk (~32%) that full-month July figures are delayed past Aug 26; (4) TRAC (July 22) noted ICE surges often fade after 1-2 weeks and fatal shootings in Maine/Texas have triggered intense scrutiny (Al Jazeera July 28), leaving ~13-15% conditional risk late-July pace drops below the 1,281/day needed to beat June. Combining ~68% chance full-month July is published by Aug 26 x ~86% conditional win rate gives July 0.59 (down from 0.62), lifting June 0.32 -> 0.39, January 0.04 -> 0.01, and holding August at 0.01.

questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.

It's not going to happen overnight'; meanwhile Philippine FM / ASEAN Special Envoy Theresa Lazaro conceded the yearly rotating envoy system has 'not really been effective' and said ASEAN is weighing a permanent envoy (signaling institutional transition rather than an imminent visit). With >55% of 2026 elapsed and zero breakthrough in Manila, 'No organization qualified' moves to 0.61.
